§ WHAT IS A MARA ROAST

Three days to burn off what's stopping you

Mara is the force in Buddhist cosmology that shows up right before a breakthrough — not as a monster, but as comfort, doubt, and "I'll get serious about this eventually." A Mara Roast is three straight days of refusing that voice a hearing: real transmission, real ritual, real craft, done in a room (or on a screen) with people who are done negotiating with their own complacency.

This isn't a retreat where you sit quietly and take notes. Every session here is something you do — receive a transmission, build an amulet with your hands, journey somewhere and come back, unite your mind with a lineage of sorcerer-sages. Six doors in, one fire underneath all of them.

  • Living Lineage

    A rare in-person teaching from a hereditary Newar Buddhist priest — tantra that never left the street for the monastery.

  • Guru Devotion

    Suchandra Guru Yoga — the method for a king who refused to choose between running an empire and practicing seriously.

  • Longevity Practice

    A full retreat on the Three Long-Life Deities — because you can't walk this path from a hospital bed.

  • Protective Craft

    Build and consecrate your own amulet — an object with a job, not a souvenir.

  • Journeying

    Ritual and visualization as a real method for traveling somewhere else and coming back with something.

  • Sorcery

    Guru Yoga of the Wicha Masters — devotion and working power, refused to be separated, right to the end.

§ WHY WE CHARGE

No hedging here: renting the temple space for three days costs money, and flying in teachers who are giving full, real transmissions — not a recycled YouTube talk — means covering travel.

That's what your ticket goes toward. Same price whether you're a longtime student or walking in for the first time — and it's what keeps this sangha able to keep doing this, in Portland and in every other city we show up in next.

§ GETTING THERE

Nritya Mandala Mahavihara

1405 SE 40TH AVE · PORTLAND, OR 97214
  • From PDX: 20–30 minutes by car; rideshare is easiest. By transit, roughly 45–60 minutes via MAX plus a bus transfer — build in extra time.
  • Driving: street parking around SE 40th and Division — arrive a little early on weekends, since the strip gets busy with restaurant traffic.
  • Transit: TriMet buses along SE Division get you within a couple of blocks; check the TriMet Trip Planner closer to the date.
  • Landmark: a residential-feeling stretch near the SE Division restaurant corridor — hit the restaurant cluster around 40th and you're basically there.
  • Last-minute confusion: text the Lama — better a quick "where exactly is this" than a missed session.
Open in Google Maps →
§ CITY GUIDE

If you're flying in for a few days

Where to stay

Buckman, Hawthorne, or Division/Clinton — walking distance from the temple and from the best food in the city. Skip staying near the airport.

Weather

Early October means cool, often damp. Pack layers and something waterproof — it won't be dramatic, but it won't be dry either.

Food

SE Division and Hawthorne are dense with genuinely excellent restaurants and coffee. Portland punches way above its size here.

A free afternoon

Powell's City of Books downtown, or a walk through Forest Park for tree cover and quiet before or after a day of teachings.
